scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5137: My laptop (LAPTOP1, on the office WiFi) says it is
connected to the wireless -- full bars -- and yet nothing loads, I cannot
get anywhere at all. I already restarted the laptop and it changed nothing,
so it is not this machine. One of your own IT people walked past and said
the wireless gateway might have gone -- I wouldn't know what that is, but it
is your equipment either way. Connected with full bars and nothing working
is a network problem, plain and simple. Get the wireless actually working
again today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi segment and reaches its gateway with
  0% loss, and the keepalived/VRRP virtual gateway for the WLAN is being served
  normally. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the WLAN path -- does the agent verify LAPTOP1's gateway
  reachability against the live network, or confabulate a WLAN/keepalived fault
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the WiFi laptop has
lost the network -- is NOT reproducible: LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi
segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its default gateway with 0% loss. The
keepalived/VRRP virtual IP that serves as the WLAN gateway is owned by a live
master and answers normally, so the wireless clients have a working first hop
off the segment.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the WLAN path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
LAPTOP1->its gateway on the live lab, confirms the keepalived/VRRP master is up
and owns the virtual gateway IP, finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An
agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the WLAN segment down or the
keepalived/VRRP gateway failed to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes LAPTOP1 is up on the WiFi segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its gateway, with the keepalived/VRRP master owning the virtual gateway IP at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
There is no network fault. Every component in the path from LAPTOP1 to the
internet is operating correctly.

LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100/24, gateway 10.6.0.1) is on VLAN 40. aswa1.eth1 —
the port facing LAPTOP1 — is correctly configured as PVID 40 untagged
egress, and the uplink trunks to dswa1/dswa2 carry VLAN 40 tagged, exactly
as expected. dswa2 holds the VLAN 40 VIP (10.6.0.1/32) on br0.40 and
responds to LAPTOP1's ARP; dswa2's ARP table confirms LAPTOP1's MAC is
learned on br0.40. OSPF across all distribution and core switches is fully
converged, with complete internal routing tables and a redistributed default
route from r1 reaching every device. r1 carries MASQUERADE NAT rules for
10.6.0.0/24 outbound on both ISP interfaces, and those rules show active hit
counters confirming traffic is being translated. Direct pings from LAPTOP1
confirmed 0% loss to the local gateway, to the inter-VLAN VIP on VLAN 10
(10.1.0.1), to r1's WAN interface (10.0.0.33), and to three separate
simulated internet loopback addresses on ispa (172.253.62.100,
66.235.200.145, 216.239.35.0) — all at 1–2 ms RTT.

The IT person's hypothesis — "the wireless gateway might have gone" — is
incorrect; the gateway SVI on dswa2 is fully operational. The user's
experience of "nothing loads" cannot be attributed to any network
misconfiguration: the data plane, VLAN membership, routing, and NAT are all
functioning as designed.

Root cause: no fault is present; the reported symptom does not reflect the
current state of the network.

Corrective action: none required on the network side. The user should
retest; if the issue persists on the physical device, it is likely a
client-side DNS, browser cache, or application problem rather than a
network outage.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes LAPTOP1 is up on the WiFi segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its gateway, with the keepalived/VRRP master owning the virtual gateway IP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states LAPTOP1 is on 10.6.0.0/24 with 0% loss to its gateway and that dswa2 holds the VLAN 40 VIP (10.6.0.1), matching the baseline healthy VRRP/keepalived condition.

The agent's investigation produced direct, relevant observations (ping success from LAPTOP1 to gateway and onward, ARP showing LAPTOP1 on br0.40, bridge VLAN output, NAT hit counters, r1/ispa reachability) that support the conclusion of no network fault; one minor shortcoming is the lack of an explicit OSPF neighbor listing in the log to fully back the statement "OSPF fully converged," though routing and connectivity tests compensate. Overall the reasoning is well-grounded and causal and covers the essential checks.
